forest_05_001.speaker: narrator
forest_05_001.text: The retort keeper began by asking everyone to stop calling the trial a demonstration. Demonstrations were arranged to impress visitors; trials were arranged to discover whether visitors should be disappointed. He had prepared two small batches from approved commercial billets, each measured at one hundred twenty kilograms of dry wood. The drying checks and scale comparison were complete. Wen sat at the sorting bench with his raised knee supported, looking delighted that disappointment had finally received an official task.

forest_05_002.speaker: narrator
forest_05_002.text: The keeper showed Lin the cold retort before loading. Its vent, closure plate, and cooling chamber were ordinary pieces of practiced construction. None would become safer because a cultivator stood nearby. He asked her to read the marked batch tags and pass them back. She did so. Then he asked her to describe the tag she had actually seen, not the one she expected. She had missed the date. He waited while she read it again.

forest_05_003.speaker: wen_cai
forest_05_003.text: He does that to everyone. My first week, I thought he had forgotten how to read and was concealing it through questions. Then I loaded the wrong pile, and he asked whether the wood had forgotten its name too. I remembered the date after that. Do not be embarrassed. He still asks my uncle. My uncle still answers as though the question is a personal insult from the entire alphabet.

forest_05_004.speaker: narrator
forest_05_004.text: The startup kindling came from the separately allocated kiln maintenance offcuts. The keeper weighed and recorded it as consumed fuel, outside the wood charged for charcoal yield. Lin liked the clean distinction until he made her carry the offcuts in two awkward baskets. Their arithmetic had handles that bit into her gloves. She set them down at the marked line and stretched her fingers. Wen offered advice from the bench, receiving the kind of look usually reserved for uninvited uncles.

forest_05_005.speaker: narrator
forest_05_005.text: The qualified crew loaded the first chamber. The billets fitted loosely enough to leave the planned channels. One worker wanted to add the last three pieces from the basket; the keeper refused because they belonged to the second weighed charge. Lin watched how a small convenience could spoil a trial without looking dangerous. Wen counted the unused pieces and found four, not three. The worker grinned and asked whether he planned to audit the keeper's lunch next.

forest_05_006.speaker: narrator
forest_05_006.text: When the fire caught, smoke rose into the cold air and flattened beneath the fir branches. The keeper adjusted the ordinary airflow under the recorded schedule. Shi Lan inspected the cleared yard and the water barrels without interfering in the kiln's operation. Her niece watched from the distant public bench with her mother, who had one remaining visiting afternoon. The girl asked whether the smoke was the forest leaving. Her mother said some of it was water, which was less interesting and more accurate.

forest_05_007.speaker: shi_lan
forest_05_007.text: A managed kiln fire and a planned ground burn have different aims. Here the keeper is limiting air to preserve charcoal. In the stand we would use a carefully bounded surface fire to reduce hazardous debris and help the approved regeneration plan. Neither task becomes wise merely because it is traditional. We check conditions and stop when they leave the plan. Today you can learn the kiln's signs. Do not borrow them later as if every fire speaks the same language.

forest_05_008.speaker: narrator
forest_05_008.text: By midday, the trial had become dull enough that several observers drifted away. The keeper considered this reassuring. He and his relief operator stayed, recording the changing vent smoke and ordinary temperatures at the designated points. Lin delivered their meal instead of asking them to eat while walking the yard. Wen's uncle arrived to watch from outside his restricted work line. His thumb was wrapped, and his jaw moved as though he were chewing every instruction he could no longer give.

forest_05_009.speaker: narrator
forest_05_009.text: The uncle asked Wen whether the knee hurt. Wen said it did. The answer surprised them both. The uncle looked at the supported leg, then at his own wrapped hand. He said he had arranged another day for the roof frame after the doctor expected to reassess him. Wen said his sister knew. For once, neither man tried to turn the other's injury into proof that somebody had been right about the foreman.

forest_05_010.speaker: narrator
forest_05_010.text: Long Qian brought a grain-house cook to observe the cooling and final weighing, not the active chamber. She had no time to wait through the whole firing. The keeper gave her the expected return interval and warned it could change with safe cooling. Long asked whether a definite time could be written into the next delivery. The keeper said yes, as a delivery target with an honest cooling condition. The cook laughed and said kitchens already understood food that refused to finish on command.

forest_05_011.speaker: long_qian
forest_05_011.text: I have spent the morning learning that a timetable can be clear without being certain. I would like to claim this as a revelation and charge someone for it. Unfortunately, the cook has been telling me for years. She says the lesson will count only when I stop punishing her helpers for a pot that boils slowly. That seems an unusually demanding examination. I intend to begin with the next wage sheet rather than another speech.

forest_05_012.speaker: narrator
forest_05_012.text: The first batch entered its sealed cooling interval that afternoon. A worker chalked the time beside the chamber and hung the keeper's closure tag. Lin copied neither the tag nor the procedure into her private practice pages. Those pages were for her own measured cultivation. She wrote only the lesson about reading the date before acting. She had already accumulated enough borrowed procedures to resemble a competent person at tasks she had never been qualified to perform.

forest_05_013.speaker: narrator
forest_05_013.text: At sunset, the niece's mother prepared to leave for her kitchen job. The child hid one mitten behind the bench, a transparent attempt to delay departure. Shi Lan found it and returned it without comment. The mother knelt to explain the next visiting date. Lin turned away, giving their goodbye a little distance. Later, the girl asked why adults could schedule fires more carefully than visits. Shi Lan said both schedules needed room for weather, then sat beside her until she cried.

forest_05_014.speaker: narrator
forest_05_014.text: The second batch was fired the following morning by a rested crew. Overnight air had grown colder, so the keeper adjusted only within the approved operating range and recorded the change. Lin took the meal turn again. Wen sorted dry fragments by the actual batch tags and earned his day's wage without hauling uphill. He complained that sitting all day made his backside heroic. His sister sent a folded cushion with a note saying the hero should stop whining.

forest_05_015.speaker: narrator
forest_05_015.text: On the next safe opening, the first chamber yielded twenty-four kilograms of dry charcoal. The second yielded twenty-six when its cooling checks were complete. The keeper weighed unusable fines separately and did not add them to saleable bags. Together the accepted charcoal filled four twelve-kilogram bags, with two kilograms reserved as an identified trial balance. The numbers were less grand than either buyer's preferred forecast. Lin watched Rong stare at them without calling them unfair.

forest_05_016.speaker: rong_sui
forest_05_016.text: One batch does not guarantee the whole stand. Two do not either. But these are approved billets at measured condition, handled by the people who will make the later fuel. I cannot reasonably insist on a higher yield because my customers would prefer it. Show me the lower planning estimate. Then show me what is already delivered, what remains standing, and what the disputed logs would have contributed. I want to stop accidentally selling the same winter three different ways.

forest_05_017.speaker: narrator
forest_05_017.text: The deputy's inventory put approved commercial wood at eighteen thousand dry-equivalent kilograms for the season, including the wood already converted and the trial charges. Twenty-four accepted bags had already left the valley. At the conservative observed yield, total seasonal output was about three hundred bags, including those deliveries and the new trial charcoal. It was a planning bound under present conditions, not a guarantee against later loss. The licensed ceiling of three hundred sixty did not manufacture the missing sixty.

forest_05_018.speaker: narrator
forest_05_018.text: The keeper emphasized that ordinary storage loss, rejected material, and a failed later firing could lower the total. The trial's second yield allowed a somewhat higher estimate, but he would not sell its upper figure as certainty. Long asked whether the remaining good timber could be burned more efficiently. The keeper showed the planned retort improvements and their modest expected benefit. There was no secret adjustment that turned the stand into four hundred eighty bags without more lawful wood.

forest_05_019.speaker: narrator
forest_05_019.text: Wen's uncle asked about the longer disputed logs. The deputy said their ownership and lawful disposition remained under review; none was counted in the approved estimate. Some might eventually be allocated as timber rather than charcoal if the decision permitted. Wen looked toward his sister's roof, then deliberately back at the scale. Lin saw the effort. Desiring a useful outcome did not make him less careful; it made the care cost him something.

forest_05_020.speaker: narrator
forest_05_020.text: The council accepted the conservative trial estimate for the allocation discussion and funded the scheduled later inventory checks. Rong would ask his town customers which existing heating stock allowed cancellation or substitution. Long would bring the completed kitchen trials and separate household heating figures. Their proposed northern extensions stayed outside confirmed supply. Lin expected another weary meeting. Shi Lan, looking toward the hollow, said they first needed to move tomorrow's gathering turn away from an animal everyone had almost forgotten.

forest_05_021.speaker: narrator
forest_05_021.text: The watch had seen both Harts at dusk near the low footbridge. The smaller one's gait was uneven, but it kept pace. The larger animal had lowered its antlers when two gatherers rounded the bend. Both people retreated without injury. Their bundles remained beside the path. Shi Lan arranged a wider daylight collection route and a qualified watch to retrieve the abandoned wood once the animals moved. A sound trial at the kiln had not made the rest of the forest convenient.

forest_05_022.speaker: narrator
forest_05_022.text: The district animal keeper's assistant arrived during the next morning's gathering turn. She carried no impressive weapon, only field glasses, a measuring cord, bandages, and a long forked barrier staff. Shi Lan met her before the narrow bridge. The assistant examined the recorded tracks and the preserved wire, then watched the hollow from high ground. She identified the animals cautiously as an adult female and a younger Hart. Their closeness suggested a related pair, not proof of it.

forest_05_023.speaker: narrator
forest_05_023.text: The younger Hart had a swollen lower leg with a dark ring near the fetlock. The assistant could see the ring through her ordinary glass when the animal stood still. It was consistent with a wire injury, though an examination at safe close range would be needed to confirm the wound's condition. She advised against forcing that examination now while the adult was alert and the youngster still mobile. Shi Lan looked relieved to be told that waiting could be competent work.

forest_05_024.speaker: narrator
forest_05_024.text: The gathered households reached the wider route in uneven groups. Some carried rope, some baskets, one a small child too tired to walk uphill. The watch explained the temporary turn and pointed to the map. An elderly man objected that the wider bend added half an hour he did not have in his knees. Shi Lan arranged the available paid carrier turn for his bundle if he wanted it. He accepted the carrying help and kept his own shorter walk within the watched approach.

forest_05_025.speaker: narrator
forest_05_025.text: Another gatherer refused to change route. Her wood was already stacked beside the low bridge, she said, and her household had no dry reserve left for the evening. The watch offered to retrieve it after the animals cleared the path. She asked when that would be. Nobody could promise an hour. Long's relief clerk authorized a measured emergency wood portion from the council stock, with the woman's own stack remaining hers. She took the portion, still angry about the delay.

forest_05_026.speaker: long_qian
forest_05_026.text: She is not being difficult for entertainment. I have argued all week that my kitchens need definite fuel. Her stove needs it too. The difference is that I can send a clerk to ask while she must stand here in the cold. Charge the emergency portion to the approved access relief, not to her later gathered bundle. If the storekeeper wants a signature, bring the page down. We can spare one pair of clerical legs.

forest_05_027.speaker: narrator
forest_05_027.text: For an hour, the revised turn worked. Families gathered from the permitted lots and returned by the wider bend. Lin helped carry empty baskets, not the wood belonging to people who had declined assistance. Wen remained at the lower sorting shelter under his knee restriction, registering the collected loads for the ordinary household allotment. He had a stool, a blanket, and an expression suggesting that all three had conspired against his reputation.

forest_05_028.speaker: narrator
forest_05_028.text: Near midday, a dog escaped from the last arriving cart. It was small, loud, and entirely sure of its importance. Its owner called it back, then ran after it when it disappeared toward the reeds. The adult Hart lifted its head. Shi Lan shouted for the man to stop. He stopped, but the dog did not. It barked at the younger animal from beneath a branch, and the adult moved between them with frightening speed.

forest_05_029.speaker: narrator
forest_05_029.text: The dog fled toward the bridge. The adult Hart followed far enough to cut across the gathering path. Its antlers caught the cart's raised side rail and tore the rail from its peg. The cart rocked. A woman stumbled against the wheel, dropping her basket. Lin and a watchman pulled her behind the stone shelter wall while Shi Lan held everyone else back. The Hart did not pursue them. It stood in the open route, flanks heaving, with the broken rail hanging from one tine.

forest_05_030.speaker: shi_lan
forest_05_030.text: Behind the wall. Leave the cart. Keep the dog here, under the blanket if it will not quiet. Nobody moves toward the youngster. The adult has an opening uphill; we need to stop filling that opening with shouting people. Lin, tell the arriving group to wait at the lower turn. Watchman, check the woman without bringing her back into sight. We will retrieve the basket when the route is clear, not while the animal is wearing part of it.

forest_05_031.speaker: narrator
forest_05_031.text: Lin went to the lower turn and found the next group already climbing. She explained the delay breathlessly, then realized her urgency was making them crowd closer to hear. She stepped into the wider space and repeated it more slowly. A man asked whether the beast was attacking houses. She said no: it stood near the bridge after a dog approached the younger Hart. That description made the people wary enough to wait without turning the incident into a village alarm.

forest_05_032.speaker: narrator
forest_05_032.text: Behind the wall, the fallen woman had scraped her palm and bruised her hip. The clinic assistant cleaned the scrape and checked whether she could stand safely. She could, with support, and accepted a short cart ride by the clear lower route once the animals moved. Her basket held eggs intended for a neighbor. Two had broken. She was furious about the eggs, perhaps because the larger fear had no useful place to go.

forest_05_033.speaker: narrator
forest_05_033.text: The animal keeper's assistant watched the adult from the high bank. She judged that the hanging rail was light enough to break loose against the branches but could still startle the animal. Approaching to remove it would be worse. Shi Lan opened the uphill exit by moving people farther down, using the barrier staff only to indicate the human boundary from a distance. No one tried to turn the staff into a lance. The adult's ears followed every movement.

forest_05_034.speaker: narrator
forest_05_034.text: The younger Hart emerged from the reeds and climbed slowly toward the wider corridor. The adult turned after it. The rail struck a forked branch and fell. For a moment the animal swung its head so violently that Lin thought it would come back toward the bridge. Then it followed the youngster uphill. The watch waited after both disappeared, listening for their return. The dog, secured under its owner's coat, made one muffled noise and received a look from everyone present.

forest_05_035.speaker: narrator
forest_05_035.text: The cart owner knelt beside the broken peg. He had kept his dog tied earlier; the worn tether had failed at its knot. He wanted the Hart's damage counted. Shi Lan said the damage would be recorded, along with the failed tether and the offered witness accounts. The emergency repair fund could make the cart usable now without deciding final responsibility. The owner accepted the temporary repair and looked less satisfied when asked to replace the tether before leaving.

forest_05_036.speaker: lin_yue
forest_05_036.text: I thought about drawing my blade when the rail broke. The thought came faster than the useful instruction. I am glad the wall was close. I would like to say I chose perfectly, but the watchman was already moving before I understood where to go. Perhaps the part I can claim is that I followed him instead of making him follow my fear. My hands are still shaking. I will give them a task that does not require a sharp edge.

forest_05_037.speaker: narrator
forest_05_037.text: She gathered the broken basket reeds from behind the wall. The woman asked for the unbroken eggs first, then accepted help arranging them in a borrowed bowl. Wen had heard the noise from the sorting shelter but stayed at his assigned post, keeping arriving children away from the narrow lane. When Lin reached him, he looked furious at his knee. She described what his instructions had prevented. He looked away as though she had tried to give him charity.

forest_05_038.speaker: wen_cai
forest_05_038.text: I wanted to be where it happened. I wanted to see whether I would be brave or useless. That is a stupid desire when someone is falling beside a cart. I know. Staying here meant I could keep three children from running to look. I did that. It felt smaller than the thing I wanted. You can tell me it mattered, and I will believe you, and I may still sulk about it for an hour. Please allow the hour.

forest_05_039.speaker: narrator
forest_05_039.text: Lin allowed it. She sat at the bench while he finished the household entries, and neither spoke until the cart owner came to collect his temporary repair receipt. The man apologized to the watch and promised a new tether. Wen wrote the receipt's location in the incident record so it would not vanish into the fuel accounts. His handwriting was firm despite his mood. A useful afternoon did not require him to enjoy every useful part of himself.

forest_05_040.speaker: narrator
forest_05_040.text: By late afternoon, the gathering route reopened on its wider turn. The elderly man received his carried bundle; the woman with the emergency portion was told when her own stack could be retrieved. The bruised woman reached the clinic and her eggs reached the neighbor. The younger Hart remained mobile in the upper corridor. Each outcome was modest and incomplete. Taken together, they kept the village from needing a heroic story to explain why people had got through the day.

forest_05_041.speaker: narrator
forest_05_041.text: At the evening meeting, the animal assistant recommended a protected movement window through the hollow, with temporary warnings and repaired household barriers. The corridor would reduce encounters, not guarantee harmless animals. The snare and antler-trade notice went to the district wildlife inquiry. Shi Lan asked for the watch costs to be funded through the next scheduled review. The buyers listened. A passage wide enough for the Harts would occupy ground that their proposed northern loading work had already assumed was free.

forest_05_042.speaker: narrator
forest_05_042.text: After supper, the niece asked whether the paper Hart should have a dog. Wen said it should have a fence and a sensible path. She found that answer boring. Lin folded a small dog anyway and tied its paper tail to a chair leg with string. The girl inspected the knot solemnly, then laughed until Shi Lan came to see what had happened. For once, the warden found an animal emergency she could solve by sitting on the floor.

forest_05_043.speaker: narrator
forest_05_043.text: The following morning, Lin found the cook examining the paper dog's tether. The cook said it was better than the rope on the flour shed, which had frayed so much that opening the door resembled fishing. Wen rose to replace that rope before breakfast. Shi Lan's niece followed with instructions of increasing complexity. He appointed her inspector of the old rope after keeping her clear of the ladder. She took the promotion seriously enough to forget to ask for jam.

forest_05_044.speaker: narrator
forest_05_044.text: Long Qian brought the remaining stove results. The tested grain-house kitchens could reduce their seasonal charcoal request by thirty bags while maintaining the usual meals, provided the repaired doors, dry mixed-fuel proportions, and paid maintenance checks continued. The reduction did not include household heating customers. The dry split wood used in the cooking mix came from the kitchens' already purchased and verified stock, outside the charcoal stand's inventory. Lin asked him to include that source in the proposal before the meeting.

forest_05_045.speaker: long_qian
forest_05_045.text: Yes. Otherwise someone will assume the household gathering lots are an invisible second storehouse. I have made that assumption often enough in other words. The kitchens have dry wood in their own shed; the keeper has checked it, and the stock was not counted in the charcoal proposal. It will be used earlier than my manager planned. That is an expense of reducing the order, even if nobody needs to buy it twice.

forest_05_046.speaker: narrator
forest_05_046.text: Rong's town messenger arrived with replies from a first group of heating customers. Some owned suitable seasoned wood and would accept a bounded cancellation of charcoal if their deposits were returned promptly. Others had no such stock and could not accept a paper substitute. The accepted cancellations totaled eighteen bags so far. Rong had authority to refund those deposits from the office's retained deposit account. He waited for the remaining replies rather than rounding eighteen into the thirty he needed.

forest_05_047.speaker: narrator
forest_05_047.text: The distinction irritated Long, who wanted the allocation meeting held before another cold night. Rong reminded him that his own stove checks had taken days. Long looked ready to answer sharply, then looked toward the cook. She was sharpening a kitchen knife on a stone with an expression of perfect indifference. He said they could meet on the stated date and make any unconfirmed cancellation explicit. The cook did not look up. Lin suspected she had heard every word.

forest_05_048.speaker: narrator
forest_05_048.text: The injured kiln worker returned to the village for a short outdoor visit, escorted by his brother. He wanted to see the trial bags. The keeper brought one to the clinic bench rather than bring him into the smoky yard. The man pressed its side and said it felt like every other sack that had ever made him tired. Then he asked whether the new drying rack would really have open shutters. The keeper said yes, and showed him the approved sketch.

forest_05_049.speaker: narrator
forest_05_049.text: His brother asked who would pay if he could not return to carrying after the next week. Rong's immediate payment did not cover an indefinite injury. The employer's claim hearing was already scheduled, and the clinic had supplied the current restrictions with the patient's agreement. Pei arranged for the worker to send his account without attending the cold office if he preferred. He preferred. His brother looked relieved and then guilty about the relief.

forest_05_050.speaker: rong_sui
forest_05_050.text: The missed-shift advance was not a promise that I would own the rest of his recovery. It was also not a trick to make him stop asking. The employer and its insurer must answer the longer claim under the work terms. My office may owe part of the loss if its delivery pressure contributed. I will provide the letters. I would like the matter settled quickly. He would probably like his breath back quickly. Neither wish authorizes a hurried settlement.

forest_05_051.speaker: narrator
forest_05_051.text: Lin carried the trial bag back with another worker. It weighed twelve kilograms, exactly enough to make its straps unpleasant by the third corner. She set it down when her grip began to twist. The worker waited without comment. In the past, she would have filled the pause with an explanation of her training or an apology for being ordinary. Today she adjusted the strap and lifted again. At the yard, the keeper asked whether she had remembered the date. She had.

forest_05_052.speaker: narrator
forest_05_052.text: Wen's knee improved under the reduced task schedule. At the clinic's next check, he was cleared for gradual return to level carrying, with steep loaded work still deferred. He celebrated by trying to stand too quickly and regretting it. His sister saw and laughed so hard that she had to put down the bowl she carried. He told her a little sympathy would improve the household climate. She said the climate had already provided enough ice for his ambitions.

forest_05_053.speaker: wen_cai
forest_05_053.text: I am going back to the yard tomorrow. I thought I would feel triumphant. Mostly I am worried the foreman will make a joke about sitting work, and I will either laugh too quickly or start another quarrel. The keeper said I can begin with him, not the foreman's uphill crew. That helps. I dislike needing it. You do not have to make the dislike disappear. Just ask me tomorrow whether I managed not to be an idiot before noon.

forest_05_054.speaker: narrator
forest_05_054.text: Lin promised the question, not the answer. She spent the afternoon assisting the deputy's inventory recheck along the licensed stand. The wood estimate included standing coppice, stacked billets, the trial charges, and material already converted. It excluded household firewood, disputed northern logs, and the four additional marked trees. The deputy showed her where uncertainty remained in moisture and usable stem condition. She liked that the estimate had a lower bound. She disliked how much labor it took to deserve one.

forest_05_055.speaker: narrator
forest_05_055.text: On a stump within the licensed stand, a small evergreen seedling had rooted in old moss. The deputy moved his boot before he crushed it. Lin asked whether the planned ground burn would kill it. He said perhaps, depending on the approved patch and heat; one seedling could not define the whole regeneration plan. Then he marked its location for the planning crew. Caring about the larger stand did not require pretending the small tree was invisible.

forest_05_056.speaker: narrator
forest_05_056.text: At the high shelter, they found two gatherers warming their hands over the permitted stove. Their wood bundles stood outside, clear of the flue outlet. One woman asked whether the migration window would keep expanding until people could no longer enter the forest. The deputy said the current restriction was local and temporary, with posted review. She asked who would attend the review. Lin named the office and date. The woman said she would come if the road remained passable.

forest_05_057.speaker: narrator
forest_05_057.text: The other gatherer remembered Harts crossing farther north when he was a boy. The upper track had since become a loading road. He could point out the old approach if his hip allowed the walk. The deputy arranged a paid witness visit by the shorter route on the next suitable day. Lin wrote the offer without promoting it to a completed survey. She had begun to appreciate the space between a useful memory and the work required to locate it.

forest_05_058.speaker: narrator
forest_05_058.text: That evening, Pei received notice that the land office would inspect the disputed segment again after the current snow eased. The engineer's retained order had narrowed the legal question, but several physical points still required confirmation. Pei folded the notice with care. Lin asked whether she was pleased. Pei said pleased was not the word for discovering how long a necessary task had waited. Then she added that she would sleep better with a date. That was close enough for tonight.

forest_05_059.speaker: narrator
forest_05_059.text: The niece asked Lin to tell her about Azure Cloud. Lin chose the small practice yard, the uncomfortable mat, and the teacher who could hear a release made too hastily from another room. The child wanted floating mountains and thunder. Lin gave her the mountain briefly, then returned to the mat. Wen listened from the doorway and said it sounded remarkably like the kiln keeper with a more expensive floor. Lin laughed until she had to admit the resemblance.

forest_05_060.speaker: lin_yue
forest_05_060.text: The expensive floor does not make the lesson easier. Sometimes I went there believing a cultivator should be beyond the small things that embarrassed everyone else. Then I would lose the return rhythm because I was hungry, or because I wanted somebody watching to admire me. There are larger possibilities in the art. I still have to reach them through the same body that dislikes cold socks. Your aunt would recognize the body immediately and send it to change socks.

forest_05_061.speaker: narrator
forest_05_061.text: Shi Lan did exactly that. The niece objected that the story had been interrupted at its best part. The warden said its best part would survive dry socks. Later, after the child slept, Lin practiced a short paired sequence indoors on the approved mat space, keeping clear of the stove and other people's bedding. She ended with the same fourth-stage structure she began with. The return was cleaner on the second attempt. It was a small improvement, useful enough without a new title.

forest_05_062.speaker: narrator
forest_05_062.text: Before bed, the cabbage farmer brought the watch a replacement bell cord. He had shortened it and braided the end to keep it from fraying. He still wanted the Harts removed from the hollow eventually. He also thanked the animal assistant for not letting the frightened adult charge through his fence. Shi Lan accepted the thanks without asking him to become an admirer. Lin watched the man's shoulders ease when nobody tried to improve his opinion along with his cord.

forest_05_063.speaker: narrator
forest_05_063.text: The next allocation meeting was posted for the following afternoon. The charcoal trial, kitchen reductions, customer replies, disputed advance, and movement corridor would all be on the table. Lin set a clean page beside her cup, then shut the notebook before she began rehearsing everyone's argument. Outside, the keeper's cooling chamber held its quiet heat. Inside, Wen was trying to mend the paper Hart without waking the niece. The antler went on crooked. He left it crooked and went to sleep.

forest_05_064.speaker: narrator
forest_05_064.text: Lin woke to the sound of a bucket being dragged across frozen ground. Wen had returned to the yard early and was trying to make the level carrying task look less like a protected assignment. The keeper stopped him before he added a second bucket. Lin asked her promised question about idiocy before noon. Wen said the day was still young. The keeper said it was young enough to begin correctly and handed him one empty pail.

forest_05_065.speaker: narrator
forest_05_065.text: The foreman passed through the yard with two workers and paused beside Wen's stool. Lin waited for the joke Wen feared. The foreman asked whether his knee could manage the western sorting shed. Wen said yes under the clinic's current limit. The foreman assigned the task at the posted rate and went on. Wen looked almost disappointed to have prepared so thoroughly for a fight that did not arrive. Lin pretended to be absorbed in the pail.

forest_05_066.speaker: wen_cai
forest_05_066.text: You may laugh now. I spent half the night inventing excellent replies. They are all useless. He only asked a question. I still remember the threat about my turn. That has not gone away because he behaved ordinarily this morning. But I would like to stop carrying tomorrow's possible quarrel on top of today's real wood. If you see me rehearsing an insult while somebody is being reasonable, spill water on my boot. A little water.

forest_05_067.speaker: narrator
forest_05_067.text: At the western shed, the workers sorted accepted sacks for the next delivery. Each saleable bag held twelve kilograms, and rejected material stayed outside the count. The trial's two-kilogram balance remained tagged for the keeper's comparison checks. Lin watched Wen record the bags already dispatched against the season total rather than add them a second time to current stock. He caught her watching and lifted his eyebrows. She said she was learning. He accepted the answer without a joke.

forest_05_068.speaker: narrator
forest_05_068.text: A courier arrived from town with the final heating-customer replies. Twelve more bags could be canceled on agreed refund terms because those customers had their own suitable seasoned stock. Added to the first eighteen, the cancellations reached thirty. No reply authorized Rong to use other households' wood. The town office had confirmed the refunds within its retained deposit funds. Rong read the authority at the gate before entering, then took off his travel gloves with unusual slowness.

forest_05_069.speaker: rong_sui
forest_05_069.text: Thirty bags canceled, deposits returned, and the remaining customers still expecting what they bought. It is a smaller promise I can actually try to keep. The town office will lose part of its margin. I would like to tell you it welcomed the honesty. It sent three pages explaining why I should have discovered the problem earlier. I agree with one of them. The other two have the virtue of being written by people who did not have to make today's visit.

forest_05_070.speaker: narrator
forest_05_070.text: Pei reviewed the received replies with the office clerk. The confirmed requests could now be reduced from three hundred sixty to three hundred: thirty canceled eastern bags and thirty saved grain-house bags. Both changes depended on terms now accepted by the affected customers or kitchens. The proposed northern extensions were still separate and unapproved. A workable plan was emerging. Its exact fit to the conservative output made Shi Lan uneasy. Winter seldom respected a plan with no spare sack.

forest_05_071.speaker: shi_lan
forest_05_071.text: We should describe three hundred as the planned seasonal supply, including the twenty-four already delivered and the trial output. We should not promise every last bag against the lower estimate without a reserve decision. A bad cooling batch or a damaged storage roof could cut the total. I want the buyers to say how they will handle a shortfall before it occurs. If the answer is 'cut north quickly,' we have learned very little from the last three weeks.

forest_05_072.speaker: narrator
forest_05_072.text: The assistant from the district animal office prepared to leave. She had arranged the next observation visit and the conditions that would justify an earlier call: worsened mobility, animals trapped near dwellings, or immediate danger to people. The local watch could report what it saw without attempting treatment. She left the barrier staff with the qualified watch under a dated equipment loan and took her glass. Lin envied the clarity of leaving a task whose next keeper was already known.

forest_05_073.speaker: narrator
forest_05_073.text: At the lower bridge, the two abandoned gathering bundles had been retrieved during the quiet period and returned to their owners. The watch found no new wire. The adult Hart's tracks stayed near the higher corridor; the youngster's passed beside them. The cabbage farmer's bell had rung once when a neighbor leaned against the fence. Everyone had looked. The farmer said the neighbor could pay for the alarm by bringing tea. The neighbor brought tea and complained that the price was excessive.

forest_05_074.speaker: narrator
forest_05_074.text: Lin took an hour of genuine rest after the morning work. She intended to read her practice pages and fell asleep instead, with the page resting against her cheek. When she woke, a line of copied characters had printed faintly on her skin. Wen's sister noticed at lunch and handed her a damp cloth. Lin asked how long everyone had been looking at the mark. The sister said only since she began explaining how carefully she organized her notes.

forest_05_075.speaker: lin_yue
forest_05_075.text: I can survive a Hart beside a broken cart and be defeated by my own handwriting. Please do not tell the child. She will ask to copy her story on my forehead, and I am not certain I have the strength to refuse while she looks serious. I will wash before the meeting. If Pei asks why I am late, you may tell her I was removing an unauthorized amendment from the official face.

forest_05_076.speaker: narrator
forest_05_076.text: Pei was not amused by the phrase, which meant she had understood it. She gave Lin the afternoon attendance sheet and asked her to bring the latest charcoal count from the yard. While reaching for the sheet, Lin noticed a small locked drawer beneath the survey cabinet. Pei pushed it shut with her knee. The motion was quick and ordinary, the kind a keeper made a hundred times. Lin had no reason yet to turn it into a question.

forest_05_077.speaker: narrator
forest_05_077.text: At the yard, the foreman refused to sign the stock count until the clerk corrected one bag that had been returned for further drying. The correction reduced current accepted stock but did not erase the bag's previous handling history. Lin thanked him. He said accurate counts should not be treated as a favor. The tone stung. She considered it later and found he was right, which did not make him pleasant. She carried the corrected count back without embellishing the exchange.

forest_05_078.speaker: narrator
forest_05_078.text: The cook prepared a pot large enough to feed the people waiting for the meeting. Long had paid the agreed ordinary preparation time, and the council bought the shared meal from its meeting expense. The cook did not need to persuade either buyer that hunger was a moral lesson. She needed an exact attendance estimate and someone to wash bowls. Lin gave her the estimate and washed until the cook said the water had grown too cold.

forest_05_079.speaker: narrator
forest_05_079.text: Wen's uncle came with his wrapped thumb tucked into his sleeve. He wanted to speak about the advance, though the foreman remained the named debtor. Pei asked what he wished to offer. He said the crew had eaten the flour and should not leave the foreman alone with it. Wen said a fair crew contribution would have to be discussed by the crew, not announced by one uncle on behalf of twelve workers. The uncle looked wounded before he looked thoughtful.

forest_05_080.speaker: wen_cai
forest_05_080.text: I am not saying we should forget the flour. I am saying you do not get to promise my next wage because you feel loyal. Ask me. Ask the injured man. Ask the two who joined after the advance was made. Maybe we can propose something together. Maybe some cannot afford it. If you sign for us now, you will have done the same thing you are trying to make honorable. I would like us to learn a less expensive kind of loyalty.

forest_05_081.speaker: narrator
forest_05_081.text: The uncle lowered his eyes, then asked whether Wen would attend a crew discussion after the meeting. Wen said yes, if the injured worker could send his answer separately. The foreman overheard and looked both relieved and irritated. He had wanted solidarity; he was receiving a process he could not control. Lin watched them find enough common ground to sit on the same bench. It was not much ground. In the cold office, it was useful.

forest_05_082.speaker: narrator
forest_05_082.text: The grain-house daughter whose pledge had been amended arrived carrying a hired load from Long's store. She deposited it at the kitchen, collected her work slip, and joined the public seating. Her father sat beside her. The household that had disagreed about its broad pledge sent its own revised proposal, which Long would review without folding it into today's fuel allocation. Lin appreciated the separate pages more now that she could recognize the people each page might otherwise swallow.

forest_05_083.speaker: narrator
forest_05_083.text: Outside, Shi Lan checked the watch change before returning to the hall. Snow had ceased, but the hollow remained white beneath the dead canopy. On the sunlit slope, meltwater already ran from the lower stones. The valley's two winters were visible at once: one held by the season, one lingering where damage had changed the ground's ordinary warmth. The coming burn plan would have to respect that difference. A single calendar date could not describe both slopes.

forest_05_084.speaker: narrator
forest_05_084.text: The meeting began with the cook's bowls still steaming. Rong placed the customer cancellations before him. Long placed the stove results. Pei placed the certified road order and the current licence. Shi Lan kept the animal report beside the corridor sketch. Lin brought the corrected stock count and sat where she could see everyone without pretending to preside. The season had become a smaller promise with sharper edges. Now they had to decide who would carry those edges when the next thing went wrong.
